newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,970 yuan ($2,888) per tonne, rising 80 yuan. It opened at 23,950 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 24,060 and a low of 23,900.
April fell 20 to 23,480, May rose 20 to 23,620, June 30 to 23,860 and August 90 to 23,950 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 24,570 tonnes from 22,940 yuan.
Copper opened slightly higher following LME gains and consolidated in a narrow range at that level for most of the session, traders said.
They said retail investors still dominated trading with many investors pushing their money into the active stock market.
"Long liquidation at high levels indicated some investors were eager to take their hot money out of the metal market," one trader said.
"There are more and more investors moving to the sidelines as the market consolidates," he added.
Traders said copper would consolidate in a narrow range in the next few days with institutional investors staying on the sidelines.
Aluminium ended down. April fell 70 yuan to 16,250 yuan ($1,958) per tonne, May 70 to 16,520, June 140 to 16,700, the first traded August ended at 16,850 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 2,300 tonnes from 400.
